images.alt: An IBM PC XT system unit photographed from the front-left angle
images.caption: The IBM PC XT added a hard drive and faster processor to the original 5150, establishing the extended architecture that defined business computing in the mid-1980s.

images.alt: An IBM PC AT system unit, viewed from above
images.caption: The IBM PC AT introduced the 80286 processor and the Advanced Technology standard in 1984, forming the hardware foundation for Windows 1.0 and Windows 3.x.

images.alt: A beige IBM PC XT tower system unit
images.caption: A complete IBM PC XT chassis, representative of the XT architecture that expanded computing beyond the original 5150.

images.alt: The motherboard and system board of an IBM PC AT
images.caption: The system board of an IBM PC AT, showing the 80286 processor and support circuitry that powered the era of Windows 3.x.

images.alt: A complete IBM PC XT system with a color CRT monitor and keyboard
images.caption: A complete IBM PC XT configuration with color monitor, as configured for business environments running MS-DOS and Windows.

images.alt: An IBM Model F mechanical keyboard with 122 keys, photographed from above
images.caption: The IBM Model F mechanical keyboard, whose legendary key feel and durability defined the user experience of DOS and Windows computing.
